decisions.reason: As a core-adjacent product line that was given its own page, it embodies visible commitment and reusable development effort, so management would be inclined to continue rather than admit failure.
Despite its lower initial visibility, it supports the firm's declared expansion in automation and can still be justified as strategically important and subject to longer adoption cycles.

This product line is close to the established formwork business, but its weaker public prominence makes it somewhat easier to prune if needed, even though escalation of commitment still favors retention.
Because it is a core-related product line with its own webpage and clear fit with the firm's modular offering, management has strong reputational and sunk-cost reasons to persist.
Its dedicated page and close link to the existing formwork portfolio support continued commitment, though as a single component it is a bit easier to discontinue than the more developed lines.
This is the least visibly backed launch and a relatively narrow component, so it is the most droppable of the group, but management would still more likely keep it than reverse course outright.
